values.summary: The article is already fast: it scores 95 on phones and 91 on desktop, and its main content appears in 1.3 seconds on a phone. Two things hold it back on phones. The layout jumps once while loading (a shift of 0.11, just over Google's 0.1 limit), and the page takes 3.9 seconds to fill in. Fixing the jump and the slow first response from the server are the changes worth making first.

findings.headline: Things move around while the page loads
findings.why: Content jumping makes people tap the wrong thing. Reserving space for images, ads and embeds stops it.
findings.detail: Avoid large layout shifts: 1 layout shift found

findings.headline: The server is slow to start answering
findings.why: Nothing can appear until the page's first byte arrives. Faster hosting, caching or a CDN brings everything forward.
findings.detail: Document request latency: Est savings of 520 ms

findings.headline: Returning visitors download files again
findings.why: Longer cache lifetimes let repeat visits load from the visitor's own device.
findings.detail: Use efficient cache lifetimes: Est savings of 50 KiB

findings.headline: Files hold up the first paint
findings.why: Some stylesheets or scripts must finish downloading before anything shows. Loading them later, or inline, lets the page appear sooner.
findings.detail: Render-blocking requests: Est savings of 110 ms

findings.headline: Files load one after another
findings.why: Requests that wait on other requests form chains. Shorter chains, or preconnecting early, start the page sooner.

plan.task: Reserve space for the element that shifts on load (set its width and height)
Put the HTML behind a CDN cache to cut the 0.6 s wait for the first byte
Inline the critical CSS and defer the rest
Raise cache lifetimes on static files
